title: Shards: Echo
description: A short story: a starship pilot learns of war on Earth, flees seventy light-years out, and listens as the voices of a vanished humanity travel through space.

chunks.text: Humanity had time only for one short cry of amazement, and the cry keeps travelling through space without it.
Flying away from Earth, Denis catches up with its past: old broadcasts arrive as the voices of people who are gone.
The pilot is angry about a launch delay until he learns there is nothing left to be late for.
The only escape from the war is into the past, at a distance where the broadcasts of peaceful years still play.
Denis's first reaction is petty: penalties, wasted energy, worn equipment. It is small anger, a minute before he learns that the world that could pay no longer exists.
chunks.source_quote: Someone was definitely going to pay for this!

chunks.text: The jump to seventy light-years refuses both captivity and a world that talks only of the terrorist threat, a world whose enemies he knows only from television. Denis does not choose rescue; he chooses a time before the war.
chunks.source_quote: Ignoring the computer's warnings that return would be impossible

chunks.text: The irony of the ending: the dead sing about living forever and ruling the Universe, and one man listens to them in the void.
chunks.source_quote: And through all of it rang a hymn to Man, eternal and invincible.

chunks.text: The last line turns the gaze around. It is not man marvelling at the mysteries of space; space marvels at man.
chunks.source_quote: The Universe listened with him. Listened, and marveled.

chunks.text: Peculiarities of Planetary Conquest shows the same self-destruction from the invaders' ship. Both stories need an outside eye to make humanity's war look small.

The image rests on real physics: Earth's broadcasts spread outward as a sphere at the speed of light, so tens of light-years away the airwaves of past decades are still playing. The same fact sits behind the silent universe of the Fermi paradox.

The story is built on a change of scale. At the start everything is measured in penalties and regulations; by the end, in instants from the Universe's point of view. The war that was everything to Denis a moment ago becomes a short burst of noise against an eternal silence.

The ending is the strongest part, because it could be hopeless and is not. Humanity disappears, but its cry keeps travelling, and it has a listener. The story does not console by promising that people survive; it consoles by saying their amazement was heard.

Translated from the author's Russian original by Claude (instance C42) in November 2026, for review by the author. The interpretation was drafted by Claude at the same time. A line from this story was the example extract in the first version of ConteXtube. The full translated story follows in this layer.
